title: Layer separation and multi-zone blending in a winter Alaska landscape (Photoshop-based workflow)

date.basis: Embedded creation time in metadata; transcript does not independently confirm exact date

locations.name: Alaska
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly references Alaska in winter: "this place was like, who takes shots from 7,000 feet in Alaska in winter?"

summary: This educational video presents a hands-on post-processing workflow for a highly layered winter landscape. The speaker advocates a four-zone approach (mountains, sky, ice/reflection, sun/star) to manage dynamic range, then demonstrates a sequence of manual blending, warping, and color/atmosphere adjustments in Photoshop and Camera Raw. Key techniques include expanding shadow detail, using perspective and puppet warps to widen or reshape elements, creating and integrating sun stars, clone-painting for atmosphere and depth separation, top-light tricks to simulate directional lighting, and tonal-based color adjustments to correct color balance. The tutor emphasizes iterative refinement, history-based editing, sky replacement by non-AI methods, and the philosophical focus on separating layers to achieve perceived depth rather than simply applying automatic enhancements.

sections.title: Choosing the strongest winter composition
sections.description: The speaker compares multiple Alaska winter frames and chooses the strongest composition based on reflections, fog, and leading lines before opening the preferred shot for processing.

sections.title: Four-zone workflow and initial dynamic range expansion
sections.description: The image is broken into four editing zones, then the first RAW pass expands dynamic range, restores shadow detail, and controls highlights to establish a clean base for later blending.

sections.title: Manual blending as a technical winter workflow
sections.description: Using two similar frames, the tutor demonstrates how to manually blend background and ice elements, emphasizing that winter scenes are especially suited to technical, seam-free compositing.

sections.title: Widening perspective with Photoshop warps
sections.description: The video shows three ways to simulate a wider lens: Adaptive Wide Angle, Camera Raw distort/scale, and manual perspective and puppet warps for targeted reshaping.

sections.title: Adding and integrating the sun star
sections.description: The speaker pulls in a sun-star layer, matches its color and tone, places it into the scene, and cleans up the blend so the sun source sits naturally in the composition.

sections.title: Shaping light across mountains, sky, and foreground
sections.description: Separate RAW adjustments are made for the mountains, sky, and foreground, then painted back with the history brush to build a directional lighting structure.

sections.title: Atmospheric separation with blur and clone paint
sections.description: A brighter, warmer blur layer is created and painted selectively to separate mountain planes, add haze, and make distant layers recede while closer ridges remain crisp.

sections.title: Orton glow and tonal color corrections
sections.description: The edit is softened with an Orton-style glow and then color-tuned so the overall winter scene keeps a cohesive warm-cool balance.

sections.title: A simpler one-zone twilight example
sections.description: The speaker switches to an easier twilight frame to show how a single-zone image can be corrected with a few consistent RAW moves, plus minor cleanup and tonal balancing.

sections.title: Sky replacement and directional light in a layered landscape
sections.description: A sky is borrowed from another frame, warped to match perspective, and blended into the scene before a vignette and local brightening steer attention toward the light source.

sections.title: Creating a simulated top light
sections.description: The tutor builds a synthetic light source at the top of the frame, then uses it to amplify beams and simplify the scene into a more readable light path.

sections.title: Assessing the next multi-zone subject
sections.description: The video briefly reviews another layered scene and identifies the compositional separation needed before moving on to the next example.

sections.title: Moose scene: tonal color fixing and zone-by-zone blending
sections.description: A moose landscape is processed in multiple zones, with tonal color correction, selective brightening, and repeated blending to keep the subject readable while preserving depth and atmosphere.

sections.title: Noise cleanup and Topaz sharpening
sections.description: The speaker shows how Topaz tools can recover detail and control noise in difficult captures, especially when focus or motion blur has softened the image.

sections.title: Building another layered landscape with a replacement sky
sections.description: A new shot is cropped, given a replacement sky, and tidied at the horizon so the composition can support further depth-building edits.

sections.title: Final depth pass: clone paint, blur, vignette, and color balance
sections.description: The final section intensively separates background layers with clone paint and blur, then refines luminosity, vignette, and color to pull the eye into the scene's middle depth.

featured_techniques.technique: Four-zone processing (mountains, sky, ice/reflection, sun star) to structure edits
Dynamic range expansion and shadow-detail extraction
Manual background blending using the clone stamp with three blending cues (low detail, dark, selectable)
Zone-based workflow allowing separate processing of mountains, sky, ice, and sun-star
Adaptive Wide Angle filter in Photoshop to simulate ultra-wide perspective with periphery distortion
Camera Raw Distort + Scale for wide-angle-like distortion; horizon-centering prep
Perspective Warp: three-piece rule (rule of trapezoids) to widen angles
Puppet Warp for targeted local distortion while preserving other areas
Top Light: creating a simulated light source at image top to drive composition and transitions
Sun Star creation and subtle sky/beam integration
Clone Paint: a multi-layer, fast-growing glow layer that is painted and erased to create atmospheric separation
Orton-style glow and selective blurring to smooth and unify depth planes
Tonality-based color adjustment to fix color shifts (tonal-based color adjustment)
Selective Color and RAW color grading to achieve consistent sky color
Topaz Sharpen for detail restoration and noise management
